latest_nl_proof:
Fix an integer m >= 2 and a tuple x=(x_1,...,x_{m-1}) of positive integers satisfying the stated inequalities. Define
S_x = {0} ∪ {q m : q ∈ N0} ∪ {q m + (m x_i + i) : q ∈ N0,
1 <= i <= m-1}.
We must prove that the genus |N0 \ S_x| equals x_1+...+x_{m-1}. Equivalently, for each residue class i with 1 <= i <= m-1, exactly x_i nonnegative integers congruent to i mod m are absent from S_x.

Observe first that every nonnegative integer n has a unique residue modulo m, so the sets of numbers in the different residue classes mod m are disjoint. Hence the complement N0 \ S_x can be counted residue class by residue class.

1. Residue class 0 modulo m.
By definition, {q m : q ∈ N0} ⊆ S_x. Thus every nonnegative multiple of m belongs to S_x, so there are no missing elements in residue class 0.

2. Residue class i modulo m, where 1 <= i <= m-1.
Fix such an i. Consider the set of all nonnegative integers congruent to i mod m; it is exactly
{i + t m : t ∈ N0}.
From the definition of S_x, the elements of S_x in this residue class are exactly
{q m + (m x_i + i) : q ∈ N0} = {i + (x_i + q)m : q ∈ N0} = {i + t m : t >= x_i}.
Indeed:
- every number of the form q m + (m x_i + i) is congruent to i mod m and equals i + (x_i+q)m, so it is of the form i + t m with t >= x_i;
- conversely, if t >= x_i, then writing t = x_i + q with q ∈ N0 gives i + t m = q m + (m x_i + i) ∈ S_x.

Now we show that no smaller number in this residue class lies in S_x. Let 0 <= t < x_i. Then i + t m is not a multiple of m because 1 <= i <= m-1, and it also cannot be of the form q m + (m x_j + j) with j ≠ i, since such a number is congruent to j mod m, not to i. If it were of the form q m + (m x_i + i), then comparing with i + t m would give t = x_i + q >= x_i, contradicting t < x_i. Therefore i + t m ∉ S_x.

So, in residue class i modulo m, the elements missing from S_x are precisely
{i, i+m, i+2m, ..., i+(x_i-1)m},
which is a set of exactly x_i elements.

3. Counting the whole complement.
The missing elements of N0 split disjointly according to their residue class modulo m. There are 0 missing elements in residue class 0, and for each i = 1,...,m-1 there are exactly x_i missing elements in residue class i. Therefore
|N0 \ S_x| = Σ_{i=1}^{m-1} x_i.
This is exactly the claimed genus formula.

Hence the genus of S_x is x_1 + ... + x_{m-1}, equivalently for each residue class i with 1 <= i <= m-1 exactly x_i integers congruent to i mod m are not in S_x. The stated inequalities on the x_i are not needed for this counting argument, but they are compatible with the definition of S_x.

Therefore the lemma is proved.
role_in_parent: Identifies the genus parameter with coordinate sum in the Kunz model.
statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2, and let x = (x_1,...,x_{m-1}) be a tuple of positive integers satisfying the inequalities: for all i,j in {1,...,m-1}, if i + j < m then x_i + x_j >= x_{i+j}, and if i + j > m then x_i + x_j + 1 >= x_{i+j-m}. Define S_x = {0} union {q m : q in N0} union {q m + (m x_i + i) : q in N0 and 1 <= i <= m-1}, where N0 = {0,1,2,...}. Then the genus of S_x is exactly x_1 + x_2 + ... + x_{m-1}, where the genus means the cardinality of N0 \ S_x. Equivalently, for each residue class i with 1 <= i <= m-1, exactly x_i integers congruent to i modulo m are missing from S_x.

domain_restrictions: m is an integer with m ≥ 2
x is a tuple of length m−1: x = (x_1,...,x_{m-1}) with each x_i a positive integer
Inequalities are conditional on comparison of i+j with m: the statement specifies constraints only for cases i+j<m and i+j>m; the case i+j=m is not constrained by these rules
In the inequality term x_{i+j-m}, the index i+j-m is understood to lie in {1,...,m-1} when i+j>m (this is satisfied given i,j∈{1,...,m-1})
S_x is constructed using q ∈ N0, so all elements of S_x are intended to lie in N0

Then the genus, defined as |N0 \ S_x|, equals x_1+...+x_{m-1}. Equivalently, for each residue i ∈ {1,...,m-1}, exactly x_i integers of the form i (mod m) are not in S_x.
quantifier_order: ∀ x_1,...,x_{m-1} ∈ Z_{>0} (subject to: ∀ i,j ∈ {1,...,m-1}, if i+j<m then x_i+x_j ≥ x_{i+j}; if i+j>m then x_i+x_j+1 ≥ x_{i+j-m})
Define S_x from m and x
